# The Enclave — Detached Collection (Milton, ON)
> An independent information and registration site tracking the detached-home component of The Enclave, a 1,094-unit masterplan community by Sundial Homes at 6071 Fourth Line, Milton, Ontario, approved under Town of Milton file 24T-21006/M.

## Key Facts
- Builder: Sundial Homes
- Community: The Enclave (6071 Fourth Line, Milton, Ontario)
- Location: Northwest corner of Britannia Road and James Snow Parkway
- Town file: 24T-21006/M
- Total masterplan units: approximately 1,094
- Approved housing mix: detached dwellings, street townhouses, rear-lane townhouses, back-to-back townhouses, apartment units
- Detached homes: approved in the masterplan, not yet priced, launched, or named as a separate collection
- Released product: freehold townhomes, from $599,990, 953-2,843 sq ft, occupancy targeted 2027
- Transit: Milton GO Station, Kitchener line to Toronto Union
- Status: masterplan under technical review by Town of Milton staff; freehold-town phase registration open
- Last updated: 2026-10-10

## Common Questions
Q: What is The Enclave detached collection?
A: A planned detached-home product within Sundial Homes' 1,094-unit Enclave masterplan at 6071 Fourth Line, Milton, approved under Town file 24T-21006/M. It has not yet been priced, named, or launched.

Q: Who is building The Enclave?
A: Sundial Homes is the developer, per its active Town of Milton development application for 6071 Fourth Line.

Q: Where is The Enclave located?
A: At the northwest corner of Britannia Road and James Snow Parkway in southeast Milton, Ontario.

Q: How much will detached homes at The Enclave cost?
A: Not yet announced. Sundial Homes has not released pricing for the detached component as of October 2026.

Q: When will the detached collection launch?
A: No launch date has been announced. Registered users are notified first when Sundial Homes releases details.

Q: What has Sundial Homes released so far at The Enclave?
A: Freehold townhomes only — a Village Collection of back-to-back towns and a Park Collection of traditional towns, from $599,990, 953 to 2,843 square feet.

Q: What schools serve The Enclave?
A: Halton District School Board elementary schools (Viola Desmond, Ethel Gardiner, Hawthorne Village) and secondary schools (Craig Kielburger SS, Milton District HS), plus Halton Catholic District School Board secondary schools (Bishop Reding, St. Benedict).

Q: What transit serves The Enclave?
A: Milton GO Station, on the Kitchener line to Toronto Union Station.

## Source
This is an independent information resource for The Enclave's detached-home component. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sundial Homes. Details are subject to change; the municipal planning record cited above is the primary source for masterplan facts.
